n:
*Translator's note:* Or “the elders,” “the ancients.”

*Translator's note:* *Grk* “were attested,” “received commendation”; and {{Hebrews 11:4|Heb 11:4-6}} shows this to be from God.

*Translator's note:* *Grk* “ages.” The temporal (ages) came to be used of the spatial (what exists in those time periods). See {{Hebrews 1:2|Heb 1:2}} for same usage.

*Translator's note:* *Grk* “by God’s word.”

*Study note:* The Greek phrasing emphasizes this point by negating the opposite: “so that what is seen did not come into being from things that are visible.”

*Translator's note:* Or “through his sacrifice”; *Grk* “through which.”

*Translator's note:* Or “through his sacrifice”; *Grk* “through it.”
*Translator's note:* Cf. BDAG 407 s.v. εὐλαβέομαι 2, “out of reverent regard (for God’s command).”

*Translator's note:* Or “settled as a resident alien.”

*Translator's note:* Or “heirs with him.”

*Translator's note:* *Grk* “past the time of maturity.”

*Translator's note:* *Grk* “power to deposit seed.” Though it is not as likely, some construe this phrase to mean “power to conceive seed,” making the whole verse about Sarah: “by faith, even though Sarah herself was barren and too old, she received ability to conceive because she regarded the one who had given the promise to be trustworthy.”

*Translator's note:* *Grk* “these”; in the translation the referent (children) has been specified for clarity.

*Translator's note:* *Grk* a collective “the sand.”

*Study note:* An allusion to {{Genesis 22:17|Gen 22:17}} (which itself goes back to {{Genesis 15:5|Gen 15:5}}).

*Translator's note:* *Grk* “the promises,” referring to the things God promised, not to the pledges themselves.

*Translator's note:* Or “sojourners.”

*Translator's note:* Here “received the promises” refers to the pledges themselves, not to the things God promised.

*Translator's note:* *Grk* “he was offering up.” The tense of this verb indicates the attempt or readiness to sacrifice Isaac without the actual completion of the deed.

*Translator's note:* *Grk* “in Isaac seed will be named for you.”

*Study note:* A quotation from {{Genesis 21:12|Gen 21:12}}.

*Translator's note:* *Grk* “having reasoned,” continuing the ideas of v. {{Hebrews 11:17|17}}.

*Translator's note:* *Grk* “in/by a symbol.”
*Translator's note:* *Grk* “worshiped on the top of his staff,” a quotation from {{Genesis 47:31|Gen 47:31}} (LXX).

*Translator's note:* *Grk* “coming to an end,” “dying.”

*Study note:* Joseph’s prophecy about *the exodus of the sons of Israel* is found in {{Genesis 50:24|Gen 50:24}}.

*Translator's note:* *Grk* “about his bones,” which refers by metonymy to the disposition of his bones, i.e., his burial.

*Study note:* The *instructions about his burial* are recorded in {{Genesis 50:25|Gen 50:25}}.
*Translator's note:* *Grk* “Moses, when he was born, was hidden by his parents.”

*Translator's note:* *Grk* “the abuse [or ‘reproach’] of Christ.”

*Translator's note:* *Grk* “he was looking away to.”

*Translator's note:* *Grk* “the pouring out of the blood.”

*Study note:* *The sprinkling of the blood* refers here to the application of the blood to the doorways of the Israelite houses (cf. {{Exodus 12:7|Exod 12:7}}, {{Exodus 12:13|13}}).

*Translator's note:* This probably refers to the righteous rule of David and others. But it could be more general and mean “did what was righteous.”

*Translator's note:* *Grk* “obtained promises,” referring to the things God promised, not to the pledges themselves.

*Study note:* *Gained what was promised*. They saw some of God’s promises fulfilled, even though the central promise remained unfulfilled until Christ came (cf. vv. {{Hebrews 11:39|39-40}}).

*Translator's note:* *Grk* “quenched the power of fire.”

*Translator's note:* Or “recovered from sickness.”

*Translator's note:* *Grk* “received back their dead from resurrection.”

*Translator's note:* *Grk* “to obtain a better resurrection.”

*Text-critical note:* The reading ἐπρίσθησαν (epristhēsan, “they were sawed apart”) is found in some significant witnesses (P46 [D* twice reads ἐπίρσθησαν, “they were burned”?] syp sa Orpt Eus). Other mss have ἐπειράσθησαν (epeirasthēsan, “they were tempted”), either before “sawed apart” ([א] L P [048] 33 81 326 1505 syh), after “sawed apart” (P13vid A D1 Ψ 1739 1881 M lat bo Orpt), or altogether in place of “sawed apart” (0150 vgmss Cl). Since the two words ἐπρίσθησαν and ἐπειράσθησαν are so much alike in sight and sound, and since the position of “they were tempted” varies in the mss, it seems best to say that ἐπειράσθησαν is an accidental transcriptional error of ἐπρίσθησαν or an intentional change to a more common word (the root of ἐπρίσθησαν [πρίζω, prizō] occurs only here in the NT, while the root of ἐπειράσθησαν [πειράζω, peirazō] occurs 38 times). The best reading here seems to be “sawed apart” without any addition before or after. (See *TCGNT* 603-4, for a discussion of emendations that scholars have proposed for this difficult problem.)

*Study note:* The expression *these all were commended* forms an *inclusio* with {{Hebrews 11:2|Heb 11:2}}: The chapter begins and ends with references to commendation for faith.

*Translator's note:* *Grk* “the promise,” referring to the thing God promised, not to the pledge itself.
*Translator's note:* The Greek phrasing emphasizes this point by negating the opposite: “so that they would not be made perfect without us.”
*Translator's note:* *Grk* “having such a great cloud of witnesses surrounding us.”

*Translator's note:* Or “disregard,” “think little of.”

*Translator's note:* Or “reproves,” “rebukes.” The Greek verb ἐλέγχω (elenchō) implies exposing someone’s sin in order to bring correction.

*Translator's note:* *Grk* “endure,” with the object (“your suffering”) understood from the context.

*Translator's note:* Or “in order to become disciplined.”

*Translator's note:* *Grk* “you are without discipline.”

*Translator's note:* *Grk* “all”; “sons” is implied by the context.

*Translator's note:* *Grk* “we had our earthly fathers as discipliners.”

*Translator's note:* *Grk* “the fathers of our flesh.” In Hebrews, “flesh” is a characteristic way of speaking about outward, physical, earthly life (cf. {{Hebrews 5:7|Heb 5:7}}; {{Hebrews 9:10|9:10}}, {{Hebrews 9:13|13}}), as opposed to the inward or spiritual dimensions of life.

*Translator's note:* *Grk* “and live.”

*Study note:* *Submit ourselves…to the Father of spirits and receive life*. This idea is drawn from Proverbs, where the Lord’s discipline brings life, while resistance to it leads to death (cf. {{Proverbs 4:13|Prov 4:13}}; {{Proverbs 6:23|6:23}}; {{Proverbs 10:17|10:17}}; {{Proverbs 16:17|16:17}}).

*Translator's note:* *Grk* “all discipline at the time does not seem to be of joy, but of sorrow.”

*Translator's note:* *Grk* “the peaceful fruit of righteousness.”

*Translator's note:* Or “straighten.”

*Study note:* A quotation from {{Isaiah 35:3|Isa 35:3}}. *Strengthen your listless hands and your weak knees* refers to the readers’ need for renewed resolve and fresh strength in their struggles (cf. {{Hebrews 10:36|Heb 10:36-39}}; {{Hebrews 12:1|12:1-3}}).
*Study note:* A quotation from {{Proverbs 4:26|Prov 4:26}}. The phrase *make straight paths for your feet* is figurative for “stay on God’s paths.”

*Study note:* The references to *peace* and *holiness* show the close connection between this paragraph and the previous one. The pathway toward “holiness” and the need for it is cited in {{Hebrews 12:10|Heb 12:10}} and {{Hebrews 12:14|14}}. More importantly {{Proverbs 4:26|Prov 4:26-27}} sets up the transition from one paragraph to the next: It urges people to stay on godly paths ({{Proverbs 4:26|Prov 4:26}}, quoted here in v. {{Hebrews 12:13|13}}) and promises that God will lead them in peace if they do so ({{Proverbs 4:27|Prov 4:27}} [LXX], quoted in v. {{Hebrews 12:14|14}}).

*Translator's note:* *Grk* “that there not be any root of bitterness,” but referring figuratively to a person who causes trouble (as in {{Deuteronomy 29:17|Deut 29:17}} [LXX] from which this is quoted).

*Study note:* An allusion to {{Deuteronomy 29:18|Deut 29:18}}.

*Translator's note:* *Grk* “that there not be any,” continuing from v. {{Hebrews 12:15|15}}.

*Study note:* An allusion to {{Genesis 27:34|Gen 27:34-41}}.

*Translator's note:* Or a command: “for understand that.”

*Translator's note:* *Grk* “it,” referring either to the repentance or the blessing. But the account in {{Genesis 27:34|Gen 27:34-41}} (which the author appeals to here) makes it clear that the blessing is what Esau sought. Thus in the translation the referent (the blessing) is specified for clarity.

*Translator's note:* This describes the nation of Israel approaching God on Mt. Sinai ({{Exodus 19|Exod 19}}). There is a clear contrast with the reference to Mount Zion in v. {{Hebrews 12:22|22}}, so this could be translated “a mountain that can be touched.” But the word “mountain” does not occur here and the more vague description seems to be deliberate.

*Translator's note:* *Grk* “a voice of words.”

*Translator's note:* *Grk* “a voice…from which those who heard begged that a word not be added to them.”

*Translator's note:* *Grk* “that which appeared.”

*Translator's note:* *Grk* “I am terrified and trembling.”

*Study note:* A quotation from {{Deuteronomy 9:19|Deut 9:19}}.
*Translator's note:* *Grk* “and the city”; the conjunction is omitted in translation since it seems to be functioning epexegetically—that is, explaining further what is meant by “Mount Zion.”

*Translator's note:* The Greek word μεσίτης (mesitēs, “mediator”) in this context does not imply that Jesus was a mediator in the contemporary sense of the word, i.e., he worked for compromise between opposing parties. Here the term describes his function as the one who was used by God to enact a new covenant which established a new relationship between God and his people, but entirely on God’s terms.

*Study note:* Abel’s shed blood cried out to the Lord for justice and judgment, but Jesus’ blood speaks of redemption and forgiveness, *something better than Abel’s does* ({{Genesis 4:10|Gen 4:10}}; {{Hebrews 9:11|Heb 9:11-14}}; {{Hebrews 11:4|11:4}}).

*Study note:* This is a vague allusion to people described in scripture and extra-biblical literature and may include Abraham and Sarah ({{Genesis 18:2|Gen 18:2-15}}), Lot ({{Genesis 19:1|Gen 19:1-14}}), Gideon ({{Judges 6:11|Judg 6:11-18}}), Manoah ({{Judges 13:3|Judg 13:3-22}}), and possibly Tobit (Tob 12:1-20).

*Translator's note:* *Grk* “as being imprisoned together.”

*Translator's note:* Or “since you too are vulnerable”; *Grk* “you also being in the body.”

*Text-critical note:* Some significant mss (א* C* P 0285vid 33 1175 1739 lat) lack καί (kai), but because the omission conforms to the wording of {{Psalm 118:6|Ps 118:6}} (117:6 LXX), it is suspect.

*Study note:* A quotation from {{Psalm 118:6|Ps 118:6}}.

*Translator's note:* *Grk* “by diverse and strange teachings.”

*Translator's note:* *Grk* “foods,” referring to the meals associated with the OT sacrifices (see the contrast with the next verse; also {{Hebrews 9:9|9:9-10}}; {{Hebrews 10:1|10:1}}, {{Hebrews 10:4|4}}, {{Hebrews 10:11|11}}).
*Translator's note:* *Grk* “whose blood is brought by the high priest.”

*Translator's note:* Or “as ones who will give an account”; *Grk* “as giving an account.”

*Translator's note:* *Grk* “that they may do this.”
*Translator's note:* *Grk* “I urge you to do this all the more.”

*Text-critical note:* Some mss (C P Ψ 6 629* 630 1505 *pm* latt syh) read ὑμῖν (humin, “in you”) here, but ἡμῖν (hēmin) has stronger external support (P46 א A Dvid K 0243 0285 33 81 104 326 365 629c 1175 1739 1881 *pm* syp co). It is also more likely that ἡμῖν would have been changed to ὑμῖν in light of the “you” which occurs at the beginning of the verse than vice versa.

*Text-critical note:* ‡ Most mss (א A [C*] 0243 0285 33 1739 1881 M latt) include the words “and ever” here, but the shorter reading (supported by P46 C3 D Ψ 6 104 365 1505 *al*) is preferred on internal grounds. It seemed more likely that scribes would assimilate the wording to the common NT doxological expression “for ever and ever,” found especially in the Apocalypse (cf., e.g., 1 Tim 1:17; 2 Tim 4:18; Rev 4:9; 22:5) than to the “forever” of {{Hebrews 13:8|Heb 13:8}}. Nevertheless, a decision is difficult here. NA28 places the phrase in brackets, indicating doubts as to its authenticity.
*Translator's note:* *Grk* “brothers.” See note on the phrase “brothers and sisters” in {{Hebrews 2:11|2:11}}.

*Translator's note:* *Grk* “Know that” (an imperative).

*Translator's note:* *Grk* “has been released, with whom, if he comes soon, I will see you.”

*Text-critical note:* Most witnesses, including several significant ones (א2 A C D H Ψ 0243 1739 1881 M lat sy bo), conclude the letter with ἀμήν (amēn, “amen”). Such a conclusion is routinely added by scribes to NT books because a few of these books originally had such an ending (cf. Rom 16:27; Gal 6:18; {{Judges 25|Jude 25}}). A majority of Greek witnesses have the concluding ἀμήν in every NT book except Acts, James, and 3 John (and even in these books, ἀμήν is found in some witnesses). It is thus a predictable variant. Further, there is sufficient testimony (P46 א* Ivid 6 33 sa) for the lack of the particle, rendering its omission the preferred reading.
